target_customer: Companies and developers building Node.js apps who pay for support, flagship support plans or studio services; Treeline targeted indie developers needing a backend
problem: Building scalable Node.js backends takes heavy coding; Treeline aimed to take coding out of building a backend, while Sails offered a ready MVC framework.
business_model: Open source framework with paid professional support and a web and mobile studio, plus a paid tier for Treeline
product_category: Open source Node.js framework and backend tooling company

founders.name: Mike McNeil
prior_employers: Balderdash (own Austin web and mobile studio)
previous_startups: Balderdash design studio, which built Sails in 2012
founders.background_notes: Original author of Sails.js and the Node-Machine Project per TechCrunch and the Sails core maintainers page.

founders.name: Scott Gress
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; no background found.

founders.name: Cody Stoltman
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; no background found.

technical_complexity.rationale: A Node.js MVC framework with an ORM is standard framework engineering; Treeline's visual backend generation on top of machinepacks was harder.

defensibility.rationale: Open source code can be freely copied and forked; value rested on maintainer expertise and community.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or copied the company; Treeline output could be hosted on Heroku per TechCrunch.

market_need_then: Node.js adoption was growing in 2012 to 2015 and Sails had been released in 2012 to serve the team's own client projects; TechCrunch in March 2015 described demand among indie developers for help building scalable backends.

branding.domain_note: Framework site is sailsjs.com; company brand is The Sails Company; Treeline used treeline.io.

identity.logo: Sails.js logo image shown in the project README

branding.community_and_virality: Sails.js is an open source project with an active GitHub community and a contributor controversy about the issue bot (single critical post, undated).

brand_strength.rationale: Sails.js is widely known in the Node.js community per the company's own description, but the company brand is thinly documented and a generic word.

outcome_analysis: The Sails Company grew out of the Sails.js framework built by Balderdash in 2012 and stayed a small studio and support business of about 4 people, with the Treeline backend tool as its venture bet in 2015. No sourced venture round, acquisition or shutdown was found, so it looks like a capital-efficient open source services company that did not scale into a large venture outcome.
notes: Funding is aggregator only: StartupIntros lists a $50K seed (2015-03) and CB Insights lists $170K total with Social Starts and YC; a $25M or $42M total attributed to Treeline in other aggregators looks like data errors or a different entity. None recorded as rounds. No outcome news found. Competitors empty because TechCrunch 2015-03 names none (Heroku is a host, not a rival). Founders Scott Gress and Cody Stoltman come from the YC page; the Sails about page now lists Kelvin Omereshone and Eric Shaw as team, not described as co-founders. The Sails Company page lists Crunchbase as organization/treeline.
